titulo: Ver, oír, oler, sentir in the imperfect = could see, hear, smell, feel
subtitulo: No veía nada. No te oía.
regla: In the imperfect, perception verbs already mean could see / could hear / could smell / could feel: No veía nada (I couldn't see anything). Poder is possible but less natural. No encontraba = I couldn't find.

bloques.texto: English needs _could_ with senses: _I could see, I couldn't hear_. Spanish uses the perception verb in the **imperfect**, with no **poder**.
**Podía ver, podía oír** are correct, but sound heavier.
**Saber** = _to taste_ works like a description: **la carne sabía salada** (_the meat tasted salty_).
Tip: in Spanish, your senses don't need permission.

lista.es: —Nos sentamos en la última fila. —¿Y ==veían== bien a los actores?
lista.en: —We sat in the last row. —And could you see the actors well?

lista.es: Tenía el radio prendido pero no ==escuchaba== nada por el ruido de las máquinas.
lista.en: I had the radio on, but I couldn't hear anything over the machines.

lista.es: Cuando tenía gripa casi no ==olía== la comida.
lista.en: When I had a cold I could barely smell the food.

lista.es: Fue horrible porque no ==sentía== la pierna.
lista.en: It was horrible because I couldn't feel my leg.

lista.es: Con el ruido de la calle no te ==oía==.
lista.en: With the street noise I couldn't hear you.

lista.es: No ==encontraba== las llaves por ningún lado.
lista.en: I couldn't find the keys anywhere.
The meat tasted a bit salty.

lista.nota: Both correct; the second is more natural.

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I couldn't see the stage._
In Spanish: _We could smell the tacos from the street._
lista.r: Olíamos los tacos desde la calle.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I couldn't find my phone._
